title: feat(core, service-messaging, service-automation, plugin-webhooks)!: webhook deliveries and the flow http node reach only public addresses unless the operator allowlists the target
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches a webhook or flow `http` node target on an internal address; the rule and its setting are stated in the changeset and the webhooks docs.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:webhook 投递和流程 `http` 节点的出站请求,现在只能到达公网地址;要访问本机或内网目标,运维需在 `OS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_TARGETS` 里明确列出;链路本地与云元数据地址无论如何都不能放行。
- 为什么改:租户可以自己填写这些请求的目标地址,原先没有任何出站检查,可以借此访问平台内部服务和云元数据。判定的是实际连上的地址(DNS 解析后、字面 IP、带 IPv4 的 IPv6 形式、每一跳重定向都判),所以 DNS 重绑定也拦得住。
- 风险与回滚:webhook 或流程原本发往内网地址的部署会被拒绝(BREAKING,changeset 有「Who moves」与一行修复:设置 `OS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_TARGETS`);发往公网目标不受影响。允许列表写错会让启动失败并列出每条错误项。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/core/src/egress/`(策略、地址分类、受保护的 fetch),`packages/services/service-messaging` 的 HTTP 投递默认 fetch,`packages/services/service-automation` 的 `http` 节点内联分支。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run src/egress`,预期 170 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地

## What changes

**Rule.** An outbound request whose target a tenant can author reaches only public addresses unless the operator's allowlist names the target. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are never reachable. The rule is judged on the address the connection is actually made to.

- `@objectstack/core/egress` (new subpath entry):
  - `EgressPolicy`: the seam, decided per connected address, host name, organization and source.
  - `createEnvEgressPolicy`: the open-core default. It admits only globally reachable addresses: every special-purpose range that is not globally reachable is refused (loopback, private (RFC 1918), carrier-grade NAT, link-local, `0/8`, `::`, multicast, broadcast and reserved, unique-local, local-use NAT64 and the rest), as is any IPv6 address outside `2000::/3`. IPv6 forms that carry an IPv4 address (mapped, SIIT, NAT64, 6to4, compat, Teredo) are judged as the IPv4 address they carry.
  - `OS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_TARGETS`: exact host names, IP addresses or CIDR blocks, comma-separated, with a strict grammar. A malformed or over-broad entry, or a link-local or metadata address, fails the boot and names every bad entry.
  - A guarded fetch: the connector resolves the host, judges every address, connects to the judged address and judges the socket's remote address again. Every redirect hop and every literal IP is judged. Where a name resolves to several judged addresses, they are dialled in turn.
  - The guard sends with its own fetch and proves at install, per guard, that its requests go through its connector. Where that cannot be proven, the install fails the boot and every send is refused before anything leaves; a response over a connection the guard did not judge is refused. The runtime requirement is stated in the changeset and the environment docs.
  - A refusal reads the same whether the target is not public or does not resolve; a policy that gives no verdict is a named refusal, never a pending request.
- **Webhooks and durable flow callouts:** the guard is the HTTP outbox dispatcher's default fetch (service-messaging). A refused target dead-letters on its first attempt as `EGRESS_REFUSED` and is never retried.
- **Flow `http` node:** the inline arm goes through the guard by a new seam (service-automation). A refusal answers `http: EGRESS_REFUSED: …`.
- **Boot:**
  - The messaging, automation and webhook plugins install the guard at init and take an `egressPolicy` option.
  - One line per policy says the guard is active.
  - plugin-webhooks logs once how many stored `sys_webhook` rows the guard will refuse.
  - The boot fails if the guard cannot be built.
- **Error-code ledger:** registers `EGRESS_REFUSED` and `EGRESS_ALLOWLIST_INVALID` under `@objectstack/core`.
- **Test fixtures:** the loopback-dialing automation suites, the showcase flow harness and one QA checklist recipe get `OS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_TARGETS` through their environment; suites that stubbed the global fetch use a named stand-in (`stubbed-fetch-egress.testkit.ts`) or an allowlisted loopback receiver. There is no `NODE_ENV` branch. The dispatcher's `fetchImpl` option is test-only and outside the rule.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/egress/egress-policy.test.ts` and `guarded-fetch.test.ts`: 170 cases covering address classes, embedded-IPv4 forms, allowlist grammar and boot refusal, connect-time judgement and re-judgement, dial-in-turn, the install-time proof, redirect hops and literal IPs.
- `service-messaging` `src/http-egress-guard.test.ts`: 10 cases (refused target dead-letters once, never retried; public target delivered).
- `service-automation` `src/builtin/http-node-egress-guard.test.ts`: 10 cases (inline arm refused, allowlisted target reached).
- `plugin-webhooks` `src/webhook-egress-census.test.ts`: 8 cases (the boot census of stored rows).

## Acceptance notes

- **Scope, as ruled:** the first wave is webhooks plus the flow `http` node.
  - Still unguarded, and named as follow-up: declarative connectors (`resilientFetch`), the OAuth grant fetches, MCP, embedders and push delivery.
  - The guard connects directly to the judged address, so an HTTP proxy configured through the environment is not used for these requests.
- **Not measured:** delivery to a real public target, because there is no direct egress in the implementing container. The public-target controls use an allowlisted stand-in.
